title: Choose the visual world for zahraasadeq.dev
question: Editorial, bold type, warm rose, as you asked. Here's the committed take. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Feature Issue
options.lineage: Design-magazine cover stories and feature spreads
options.thesis: The site is a magazine issue about Zahraa: a cover, then each product as a full feature story with folios, deks and pull quotes.
options.viewport: Cover: ZAHRAA SADEQ set edge to edge on a full rose field, with cover lines (Nesvia, Swazona Media, From Raytheon to AI) and an 'Issue 2026' masthead. Résumé and email sit as the cover price/barcode corner.
options.risk: Can feel like a costume if the magazine devices (folios, issue numbers) are applied without real editorial hierarchy.

raised.raise: Every display line is fitted to fill the full measure, never floating at a timid size.
A single running folio line tracks where you are in the issue, like a chase light across the page.
Link and state are drawn in stroke (underline weight, rule breaks), never by hue alone.

options.label: The Model Card
options.lineage: arXiv papers and ML model cards
options.thesis: Zahraa presented as a research paper: abstract, figures, tables, each product a numbered section with real architecture diagrams.
options.viewport: Title block with name, affiliations (Raytheon, U of Arizona), an abstract, and Figure 1: the Nesvia scoring pipeline.
options.risk: The most familiar 'AI engineer' look, and less bold than the editorial direction you asked for.

options.label: Wood-Type Broadside
options.lineage: Hatch Show Print letterpress gig posters
options.thesis: One tall broadside: name, products and experience stacked as full-width wood-type bands.
options.viewport: ZAHRAA SADEQ / AI ENGINEER / NOW SHOWING: NESVIA, stacked in carved bands.
options.case: Very strong bold-type energy, but a gig poster says 'music' louder than 'AI engineer'.
options.risk: Reads nostalgic and crafty rather than technical.

options.label: Step Sequencer
options.thesis: Career as a 16-step pattern under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A step row where each lit key is a project.
options.case: Playful, but hiring managers don't recognize themselves in it.
options.kept: The single running line that always shows where 'now' is.

options.label: Patchbay Schedule
options.thesis: Numbered amber lanes on black glass.
options.viewport: Lanes 01-48 with each project tied to its stack.
options.case: Too cold, and drops the rose you asked for.
options.kept: State is drawn by stroke pattern, not color.

options.label: Multiplane Dawn
options.kept: Scroll-linked depth: layers moving at different speeds.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, modern developer portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name, one-line role, CTA buttons, then a project grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other portfolios by design.
